thammanna is arrested in the corridor on the registered-document offence, and his name is spelled aloud twice — once into the enquiry record and once on the arrest memo.

mallesha refuses to look at the photograph and leaves for school before six.
thammanna leaves the receipt book open on the step; chaitra counts 288 entries of twelve hundred rupees each, every one signed by her father in an unfamiliar hand, the earliest predating her birth.

ratnamma produces the only print of the 16 July 1994 wedding photograph, in which mallesha stands behind the groom holding the garland; chaitra learns the two men were brothers.

mallesha states in eleven sentences that the house was mortgaged for thirty-eight thousand rupees for the marriage, that the appointee died before joining so nothing was payable, and that a block office clerk came in September 1994 and told him the date column of a joining report is written by a clerk.

chaitra names the shame she has carried since she was eight — that she told people her father was a coward for never standing for a photograph — and mallesha explains the avoidance in one sentence about newspapers reaching the block office.
chaitra opens the cloth pouch and finds that column four of her own birth certificate, registered 14 January 2000, names lokanath as her father.

inchara introduces herself and reveals she has held a photocopy of the Nerlige family tree register since 2019 and has done nothing with it while waiting for someone from that house to become angry in a government building.
chaitra files form fifteen for correction of the father's name in the birth register and says the name mallesha aloud in a government office for the first time since 1994.

thammanna states his price — the four acres mutated to his son-in-law and a resignation signed in the dead name by the fifth of next month — and enters the correction application in the inward register as received from 'daughter of Lokanath'.

chaitra intercepts revanna between the chair and the car; he orders her file reopened and directs that the reason be read out at the counter, and states that an anonymous 2019 complaint from that taluk was returned to him marked no irregularity over puttaraju's signature.
basavaraj reads the reopening order aloud to the same corridor of ninety people and addresses chaitra as madam.
The movement register shows mallesha's district service file was requisitioned at 09:20 that morning by thammanna, purpose recorded as pre-audit scrutiny.
mallesha writes a voluntary retirement letter on false medical grounds and signs it in the dead name, intending to meet thammanna's terms and clear his daughter's file.

shankarappa refuses to forward the resignation and states that he compared the joining photograph with the man in 2011, saw they were different men, locked the register and said nothing for eleven years.

Before school that morning shankarappa posted, by registered acknowledgement due from a post office outside his own village, a statement to revanna naming which man has signed the Nerlige staff attendance register since 1998 and admitting his own eleven-year silence.

forbidden.location: Nerlige school, gate and assembly ground
forbidden.fact: ratnamma demands in the school yard that mallesha say his own name once and she will tear up the petition; he answers with the fourth standard timetable and walks to his classroom.

A claim petition for forty-one lakh sixty thousand rupees is served at the school gate at assembly time, naming the department as first respondent and savithri as second; ratnamma privately tells chaitra she wants a paper and not the money, and gives her until the hearing on the twenty-second.
seetharama produces volume four of his seva register; the entry of 16 July 1994 records the marriage, and records that the dakshine was paid by the groom's younger brother.

Under rule sixty-one revanna accepts the temple record plus two attesting statements — from the bride's uncle and from girija, who attended the 1994 marriage — and sanctions family pension to ratnamma, arrears referred to government.

Four lines below the marriage entry, the seva register records the funeral rites of 25 August 1994 — eighty fed, sixteen hundred and one rupees — with the payer's column filled in the name of thammanna, three weeks before he claims he was first deputed to the village.
puttaraju states he signed the 2019 nil report without reading it, one of sixty-one files signed that day; shankarappa admits article two orally in front of his own staff.

Sale deed number 1147 conveying the four acres by the canal is registered on the strength of the 2011 general power of attorney; no member of the family is present and none learns of it for fifteen days.

thammanna's recorded statement casts him as the 2019 informant and a reluctant recipient of a bribe paid by the family for twenty-four years; he produces the receipt book counterfoils and denies the temple entry as a priest's book.
inchara hands over the recovery notice for one crore eleven lakh forty thousand rupees and the office file copy of the 2019 complaint, whose covering slip is signed by thammanna.

bible.want: To meet every stranger at the threshold, give the household its safe script, and end the visit before anyone says the wrong name.
bible.wound: Savithri knowingly avoids questions that would force the household's lie into the open, substituting food, money, and practical rescue for honest answers. It keeps the house functioning, but teaches her children not to confide in her and teaches opportunists that she can be made useful if they threaten to speak.
bible.voice: With guests or family, she speaks in short imperatives: sit, eat, drink, go. Her specific deflection is hospitality—when uncomfortable, she changes the subject to food, water, seating, illness, or whether a child has eaten. When forced to account for herself, her sentences become long chronological inventories of ages, sums, objects, and who stood where; she repeats a clause until it steadies her. When frightened, she first gives a household order or uses a formal kinship address, then turns flat; if neither works, her voice cracks rather than grows louder.
bible.engine: Savithri is the household's human buffer: relatives, neighbors, creditors, and strangers learn that she will trade a meal, an errand, cash, labor, or a favor for letting a dangerous question drop. Every successful deflection attracts another demand, adds another debt, and deprives her of information she has effectively paid not to hear. Because food, illness, credit, ceremonies, and visitors never stop, the bargain renews itself daily and becomes harder to control each time it works.

offscreen_ledger.window: between the season opening and b004
offscreen_ledger.what: She moves old envelopes from the front room to the kitchen loft; returns borrowed coffee cups to three households; and cooks a second pot of rice for visitors she expects but does not discuss.
She gathers the flowers scattered outside the gate and scrubs away the red powder; then returns the borrowed serving vessels without explaining why they were barely used.
She measures the rice left in the tin; accepts three paid lunch orders; cooks and packs the meals before sunrise; and uses the coins to buy the next sack on credit.

She accepts a feast order; borrows two cauldrons; buys lentils on credit; sends prakash for firewood; grinds spices; cooks through the night; delivers the pots before dawn; collects half the promised payment; pays the grocer; carries the leftovers to an ill neighbor; redirects questions in the lane into an argument about the recipe; retrieves the borrowed vessels; and replaces a missing lid with one from her own kitchen.

She pours away the coffee that has gone cold; wraps the untouched twelve hundred rupees in cloth; returns it to the rice tin; and pays the grocer from her cooking earnings rather than disturb the bundle.
She washes the cup ratnamma used and places it with the family's cups; then lays a second plate beside the household plates before the next meal.
She opens the metal box, removes the paper she signed in 2011, and carries it folded to the corridor without reading it to the end.
She buys water for the waiting family; then opens the food bundle she brought and portions it among them.

bible.reframe: The mainline is about a false public identity collapsing under official scrutiny; Savithri's serial is about domestic care turned into a system of censorship, and a woman who keeps choosing to be useful so that she will not have to be fully informed.
bible.pitch: A wife who can silence almost any question with a meal keeps feeding the people who are learning exactly what her silence is worth.

episode.title: The Second Plate
episode.logline: When Ratnamma returns to the veranda, Savithri offers money, coffee, and food to prevent another public question—but the woman answers with a mercy Savithri cannot explain.
episode.script:
SFX: A motorcycle approaches, slows near the gate, then accelerates away.

NARRATOR: On the seventh, Savithri stood at the threshold with twelve hundred rupees wrapped in a handkerchief. For the first time in twenty-four years, Thammanna rode past without stopping.

SAVITHRI: Sir! Coffee is ready.

SFX: The motorcycle fades.

SAVITHRI: Mallesha, call him back.

MALLESHA: No.

SAVITHRI: He may not have seen me. The sun is in his eyes at this hour. Call him.

MALLESHA: The audit team sat on the fifth. He handed nothing over.

SAVITHRI: Drink your coffee before it cools.

MALLESHA: Savithri—

SAVITHRI: Drink it.

SFX: A metal tumbler touches the veranda ledge.

MALLESHA: He has never missed the seventh.

SAVITHRI: Then it is not the seventh any more. It is something else.

SFX: Savithri's footsteps hurry into the house. A door curtain snaps behind her.

SFX: Cold coffee pours into a sink. Coins and folded notes rustle.

NARRATOR: Savithri returned the twelve hundred rupees to the rice tin. She was frightened, so she measured rice. Eleven measures remained. Numbers behaved better than visitors.

SFX: A tin lid closes. Knuckles rap against the open doorframe.

KAMALAMMA: Savithri! Are the lunch carriers ready?

SAVITHRI: Sit. I will pack them.

KAMALAMMA: We can stand. Shobha and Leela are waiting at the gate.

SHOBHA: We are here, Savithri.

LEELA: We can hear everything.

SFX: Three steel carriers are placed on the floor.

SAVITHRI: Rice, lentils, beans. Return the carriers tomorrow.

KAMALAMMA: You promised curd.

SAVITHRI: I will send it.

KAMALAMMA: And two hundred rupees back.

SAVITHRI: The price was agreed.

KAMALAMMA: Before Ratnamma questioned your husband in the lane. Everyone heard her ask what she is to him. Now my mother-in-law says food from this house comes with stories.

SHOBHA: Kamalamma, leave it.

KAMALAMMA: Why? Savithri wants people to leave things. That has a price too.

SFX: A lunch-carrier latch clicks open.

SAVITHRI: Do not open it here.

KAMALAMMA: Then return two hundred.

NARRATOR: Savithri was ashamed. Two women were at the gate, one woman was inside her kitchen, and all three were waiting to learn the price of her silence.

SFX: Coins counted onto steel. One, two, three, four.

SAVITHRI: Fifty each. Two hundred. Take the food and go.

KAMALAMMA: Say it properly. You are reducing the price because I will not repeat Ratnamma's question.

SAVITHRI: The beans cost less this week.

KAMALAMMA: Say it.

SAVITHRI: Take the curd also.

KAMALAMMA: Savithri—

SAVITHRI: Take it and go!

SFX: Nothing. Long.

SHOBHA: She paid you in front of us, Kamalamma. That should be enough humiliation for one lunch.

SFX: Steel carriers lift. Three pairs of sandals retreat.

KAMALAMMA: Tell your daughter to bring the curd.

SAVITHRI: Tell your mother the huli was good this year.

SFX: Savithri shuts the door.

SFX: A lane crowded with murmuring neighbors. A walking stick strikes the veranda step once.

NARRATOR: By late afternoon, Ratnamma stood outside the house again. Savithri saw faces at three gates and shadows behind two windows. She wanted to close the door, but Ratnamma's walking stick was already across the threshold line.

SAVITHRI: Ratnakka. Sit. I will bring coffee.

RATNAMMA: No.

SAVITHRI: You have come in the heat. Sit.

RATNAMMA: I did not come for coffee.

SAVITHRI: There is rice. There is huli from yesterday. It is better today.

RATNAMMA: I did not come for food.

SAVITHRI: Then water. Prakash! Bring water.

RATNAMMA: No water.

SFX: The lane murmurs more loudly.

LANE WOMAN: Ask her now, Ratnamma!

LANE MAN: Let the whole lane hear the answer this time.

SAVITHRI: Do not shout from the road. If you want water, come and drink it.

RATNAMMA: Savithri, look at me.

SAVITHRI: The rice will catch at the bottom.

RATNAMMA: Look at me.

SFX: The kitchen fire crackles through the doorway.

NARRATOR: Savithri was terrified. She had fed wedding guests, funeral guests, creditors, fevered children, and women who came only to count the vessels in her kitchen. She knew how much rice ended a visit. She did not know what ended this one.

SFX: Cloth unfolds. Currency notes rustle in Savithri's hand.

SAVITHRI: This is twelve hundred rupees. It was kept for the seventh. Take it. Buy medicines, grain, anything. Take it and do not stand in the lane.

RATNAMMA: Put it away.

SAVITHRI: It is twelve hundred. Count it.

RATNAMMA: I said put it away.

SAVITHRI: Ratnakka, I was nineteen when I came here, and from that day I have served whoever stood at this door. I served you when you came. I served the people who came to watch you. I have not asked which paper was carried where or why one person stopped coming on the seventh. I am asking only this: eat first, and whatever must be said can be said without the lane listening.

RATNAMMA: No.

SAVITHRI: Then tell me the amount.

RATNAMMA: This is not an amount.

SAVITHRI: Everything becomes an amount when it enters a house.

RATNAMMA: Not this.

SFX: Ratnamma's walking stick turns against the stone. The lane falls quiet.

RATNAMMA: Listen, all of you. I withdraw the claim as against Savithri.

SFX: Several neighbors gasp. A child repeats the word “withdraw.”

LANE WOMAN: Against Savithri?

RATNAMMA: Against Savithri.

LANE MAN: Say why.

RATNAMMA: I have said what I came to say.

SFX: The currency slips from Savithri's hand onto the veranda.

SAVITHRI: (and something in it cracks) She has withdrawn it against me!

KAMALAMMA: We heard her, Savithri. Ratnamma has withdrawn it against you.

NARRATOR: The same neighbor who had priced Savithri's silence that morning now spoke her release to the lane. Savithri was relieved, but the relief hurt. Ratnamma had refused her money, her coffee, her food, and every reason Savithri knew how to offer.

SAVITHRI: Ratnakka. Come inside.

RATNAMMA: Inside?

SAVITHRI: Prakash, move the sandals. Bring water. Wash the steel cup, not the glass one. Ratnakka, come inside.

SFX: One step crosses the threshold. Then another. The walking stick follows.

SFX: A steel cup fills with water. A plate is set on the floor beside another plate.

NARRATOR: Savithri took Ratnamma inside the house. She did not ask why the claim had been withdrawn. Asking might have changed the answer, and Savithri had spent her life rescuing answers before they could change.

SAVITHRI: Sit. Drink. I will heat the rice.

RATNAMMA: I said I am not hungry.

SAVITHRI: Nobody comes inside this house and leaves without eating.

RATNAMMA: You have a rule for everything.

SAVITHRI: Rice first. Then speak.

SFX: A ladle scrapes the bottom of a pot. Rice falls onto the second plate.

RATNAMMA: Why are you giving me a family plate?

SAVITHRI: The guest plates are not dry.

RATNAMMA: That is not true.

SAVITHRI: Eat.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

SAVITHRI: Ratnakka, eat.

RATNAMMA: This is the first time I have entered this house in twenty-eight years.
